title: Cristaux et cohomologie de De Rham : généralités, correspondances Deligne et Berthelot (1965-1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is a typed sheet, photographed upside down, numbered '34' (with '6' in the corner). It does not look like Grothendieck's own manuscript notes. It is written in Weil's 'Foundations' language: generic points over fields K(a_0,...), points written as products a_0×a_1×..., and the reference [14] IX §2 Th.3, which is very likely Weil's Foundations of Algebraic Geometry, ch. IX (divisors of functions and their intersections with fibres). It is probably part of a thesis or article on abelian varieties that was filed in this folder. The neighbouring pages, on Witt-vector divided-power-type relations and v_p(n!), are unrelated.

The mathematics:
(1) There is a divisor D on B = A^5, for an abelian variety A, and a rational function g on B. The earlier relation (D − div(g))·(w_1×…×A×…×w_5) = 0 says that D − div(g) has zero intersection with every fibre in which the h-th factor is A and the other coordinates are generic points w_i.
(2) Suppose D − div(g) ≠ 0 and let Z be a component. Then Z would project onto a subvariety of codimension ≥ 2 in each of the five 4-fold partial products. That is impossible: Z has dimension 5g−1 and its fibres over A^4 have dimension at most g, so its image has dimension at least 4g−1, i.e. codimension at most 1. Hence D = div(g).
(3) Take z generic on A over K(a_0,a_1,a_2,b_0) and set g'(z) = g(a_0,a_1,a_2,b_0,z). Weil's theorem on restricting a divisor of a function to a slice gives a_0×a_1×a_2×b_0×div(g') = div(g)·(a_0×a_1×a_2×b_0×A). By the explicit form of div(g) and a 'Lemme 2', this equals a_0×a_1×a_2×b_0×X_ā. Hence div(g') = X_ā, a divisor on A depending on the parameter ā.
(4) The points c (presumably a_0×a_1×a_2×b_0×b_1) and c_0 = a_0×a_1×a_2×b_0×b_0 lie off the support of div(g). So g(c) = g'(b_1) and g(c_0) = g'(b_0).
(5) A cocycle/normalisation identity: g(x_0,x_1,x_2,y_1,ȳ_1) = g(x_0,x_1,x_2,y_0,ȳ_1)·g(x_0,x_1,x_2,y_0,y_1)^{-1}.

This is the classical Weil-style technique of building functions with prescribed divisors on products of abelian varieties via the theorem of the cube/square. It serves something like the construction of a pairing (e.g. a Weil-pairing or Picard-variety argument) evaluated through function values at points.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The codimension argument is correct for dim A ≥ 1, though stated tersely.
The page appears misfiled: it is a typed Weil-style text on abelian varieties, not part of Grothendieck's handwritten notes on crystals/De Rham cohomology. Authorship is unsure.

ideas.what: Showing D = div(g) on A^5 by checking that D − div(g) vanishes on all fibres and using a dimension count on projections to the 4-fold partial products
ideas.modern_name: Seesaw/rigidity-type argument for divisors on products of abelian varieties

ideas.what: Restricting div(g) to a slice a_0×a_1×a_2×b_0×A to get a function g' with div(g') = X_ā, then evaluating at points
ideas.modern_name: Restriction of principal divisors to fibres (Weil, Foundations IX §2 Th.3)

ideas.what: Multiplicative cocycle identity g(…,y_1,ȳ_1) = g(…,y_0,ȳ_1) g(…,y_0,y_1)^{-1}
ideas.modern_name: Normalised function/cocycle relation (theorem of the square/cube type)
